title: Finite-order homogeneous correction for a nondegenerate binary quadratic
statement: Let $F$ be a field, $S=F[[u,v]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], $\mathfrak p=(u,v)$, and $Q(U,V)=aU^2+bUV+cV^2$ for $a,b,c\in F$ with $b^2-4ac\ne0$. Put $L_1=2au+bv$ and $L_2=bu+2cv$. Let $r\ge2$, $f,x,y\in S$, $x-u,y-v\in\mathfrak p^2$, and $E=f-Q(x,y)\in\mathfrak p^{r+1}$. Let $H\in F[u,v]$ be the homogeneous degree-$(r+1)$ component of $E$ (the sum of its monomials of that total degree). There exist homogeneous polynomials $A,B\in F[U,V]$ of degree $r$ (zero is allowed) such that $H=L_1A(u,v)+L_2B(u,v)$. For these choices, putting $x'=x+A(x,y)$ and $y'=y+B(x,y)$, one has $x'-x,y'-y\in\mathfrak p^r$, $x'-u,y'-v\in\mathfrak p^2$, and $Q(x',y')-Q(x,y)-H\in\mathfrak p^{r+2}$, hence $f-Q(x',y')\in\mathfrak p^{r+2}$. No restriction on the characteristic of $F$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0C49 (lemma-nodal-algebraic), proof of (2) implies (3), polar-basis correction modulo the fourth power and its induction to higher powers; the same calculation with fixed series f and error f-Q(x,y).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-combined-ideal-coefficients] with $\Lambda=F$, $J=0$ and $d=2$. For $n\ge1$ it says exactly that membership in $\mathfrak p^n$ is vanishing of every coefficient of total degree $<n$, because $0^{n-|E|}=0$ for $|E|<n$. Thus $E$ has no terms below degree $r+1$. Subtracting its finite degree-$(r+1)$ part $H$ leaves no terms below degree $r+2$, so $E-H\in\mathfrak p^{r+2}$. There are only $r+2$ binary monomials of degree $r+1$, so $H$ is indeed a polynomial.

source.place: Tag 0C49 (lemma-nodal-algebraic), proof of (2) implies (3), polar correction formula and higher-order induction; explicit fixed-series version.

proof.text: Write $H=\sum_{i+j=r+1}h_{ij}u^iv^j$. Define $P(U,V)=\sum_{i+j=r+1,\ i>0}h_{ij}U^{i-1}V^j$ and $R(U,V)=h_{0,r+1}V^r$. Then $H=uP(u,v)+vR(u,v)$, and both $P,R$ are homogeneous of degree $r$. Put $D=4ac-b^2\ne0$ and set $A=D^{-1}(2cP-bR)$, $B=D^{-1}(-bP+2aR)$. Multiplication gives $2aA+bB=P$ and $bA+2cB=R$. Therefore $L_1A(u,v)+L_2B(u,v)=H$. All these are polynomial identities; the inverse used is only that of the nonzero field element $D$. The zero polynomial is permitted throughout.

source.place: Tag 0C49 (lemma-nodal-algebraic), proof of (2) implies (3), polar correction formula and higher-order induction; explicit fixed-series version.

proof.text:
The hypotheses imply $x,y\in\mathfrak p$. For any degree-$r$ monomial $U^iV^j$ one has $x^iy^j\in\mathfrak p^r$. Moreover
$$x^iy^j-u^iv^j=(x^i-u^i)y^j+u^i(y^j-v^j)\in\mathfrak p^{r+1}.$$
Indeed, if $i>0$, then $x^i-u^i=(x-u)\sum_{k=0}^{i-1}x^{i-1-k}u^k\in\mathfrak p^{i+1}$; for $i=0$ the difference is zero. The corresponding formula for $y^j-v^j$ gives order $j+1$ when $j>0$. Multiplying by the other $j$ or $i$ factors gives the stated order. Summing the finitely many monomials of $A,B$ proves, for $\delta=A(x,y)$ and $\epsilon=B(x,y)$, that $\delta,\epsilon\in\mathfrak p^r$ and $\delta-A(u,v),\epsilon-B(u,v)\in\mathfrak p^{r+1}$.

source.place: Tag 0C49 (lemma-nodal-algebraic), proof of (2) implies (3), polar correction formula and higher-order induction; explicit fixed-series version.

proof.text:
Set $x'=x+\delta$, $y'=y+\epsilon$. Then $x'-x,y'-y\in\mathfrak p^r$. Since $r\ge2$, both differences also lie in $\mathfrak p^2$, hence $x'-u,y'-v\in\mathfrak p^2$. Write $M_1=2ax+by$ and $M_2=bx+2cy$. We have $M_i\in\mathfrak p$ and $M_i-L_i\in\mathfrak p^2$. Consequently
$$M_1\delta-L_1A(u,v)=(M_1-L_1)\delta+L_1(\delta-A(u,v))\in\mathfrak p^{r+2},$$
and likewise $M_2\epsilon-L_2B(u,v)\in\mathfrak p^{r+2}$. Here every estimate is just multiplication of ideal powers, $\mathfrak p^s\mathfrak p^t\subseteq\mathfrak p^{s+t}$. Adding and using step 2 gives $M_1\delta+M_2\epsilon-H\in\mathfrak p^{r+2}$.

source.place: Tag 0C49 (lemma-nodal-algebraic), proof of (2) implies (3), polar correction formula and higher-order induction; explicit fixed-series version.

proof.text:
Direct expansion of the quadratic gives the exact identity
$$Q(x',y')-Q(x,y)=M_1\delta+M_2\epsilon+a\delta^2+b\delta\epsilon+c\epsilon^2.$$
The last three terms lie in $\mathfrak p^{2r}\subseteq\mathfrak p^{r+2}$, since $r\ge2$. Step 4 therefore gives $Q(x',y')-Q(x,y)-H\in\mathfrak p^{r+2}$. Finally
$$f-Q(x',y')=(E-H)-(Q(x',y')-Q(x,y)-H)\in\mathfrak p^{r+2}$$
by step 1. The expansion and all ideal inclusions hold in every characteristic, proving every claimed clause.

lean.statement: theorem exists_binary_quadratic_order_correction (F : Type u) [Field F] (a b c : F) (hdisc : b ^ 2 - 4 * a * c ≠ 0) (Q : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) F) (hQ : Q = MvPolynomial.C a * MvPolynomial.X 0 ^ 2 + MvPolynomial.C b * MvPolynomial.X 0 * MvPolynomial.X 1 + MvPolynomial.C c * MvPolynomial.X 1 ^ 2) (p : Ideal (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) F)) (hp : p = Ideal.span (Set.range (X : Fin 2 → MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) F))) (r : ℕ) (hr : 2 ≤ r) (f x y : MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) F) (hx : x - X 0 ∈ p ^ 2) (hy : y - X 1 ∈ p ^ 2) (hE : f - MvPolynomial.aeval ![x, y] Q ∈ p ^ (r + 1)) (H : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) F) (hH : (H : MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) F) = homogeneousComponent (r + 1) (f - MvPolynomial.aeval ![x, y] Q)) : ∃ A B : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) F, A.IsHomogeneous r ∧ B.IsHomogeneous r ∧ (H : MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) F) = ((2 * a) • X 0 + b • X 1) * (A : MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) F) + (b • X 0 + (2 * c) • X 1) * (B : MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) F) ∧ ∀ x' y' : MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) F, x' = x + MvPolynomial.aeval ![x, y] A → y' = y + MvPolynomial.aeval ![x, y] B → x' - x ∈ p ^ r ∧ y' - y ∈ p ^ r ∧ x' - X 0 ∈ p ^ 2 ∧ y' - X 1 ∈ p ^ 2 ∧ MvPolynomial.aeval ![x', y'] Q - MvPolynomial.aeval ![x, y] Q - (H : MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) F) ∈ p ^ (r + 2) ∧ f - MvPolynomial.aeval ![x', y'] Q ∈ p ^ (r + 2)
